title: A Friendly Game of Bingo
description: Find the words for a familiar American bingo session, from the caller’s numbers to the marks on a card.
cardDescription: Find the words for a familiar American bingo session, from the caller’s numbers to the marks on a card.
focus: Bingo formats vary. These clues refer to the familiar American card game while separating the person announcing numbers, the marking tool, and the possible lines on a card.
solvingTip: A clue may name the player’s equipment, an arrangement of squares, or a role. Read the category before choosing a short game word.
words: Number-matching game in which players mark spaces on cards
Ink marker commonly used to mark a bingo card
Person announcing the drawn bingo numbers
Line running from one corner toward the opposite corner
Word on the center space of many American bingo cards
Printed grid on which a bingo player marks numbers
Value announced after a bingo ball is drawn
Horizontal line of spaces on a bingo card
Vertical line of spaces on a bingo card
To identify a called space on one's card
Individual square within the card's grid
To satisfy the announced pattern before competing players
Organized round played under stated rules
Numbered sphere drawn in a traditional bingo session

answerNotes.BINGO: American bingo commonly uses a 75-ball format. Other formats exist, so a feature of one version is not a rule for all bingo.
answerNotes.DAUBER: A dauber marks the selected spaces. Some players instead use counters or electronic versions.
answerNotes.CALLER: The caller announces results of the draw. That role is separate from the players marking their own cards.
answerNotes.DIAGONAL: A diagonal differs from a horizontal row or a vertical column. Which patterns win depends on the round's announced rules.
answerNotes.FREE: Many standard American cards have a free center space. Other bingo formats do not necessarily use that layout.

title: A Round of Shuffleboard
description: Compare the familiar words for court and table shuffleboard through their equipment and sliding motion.
cardDescription: Compare the familiar words for court and table shuffleboard through their equipment and sliding motion.
focus: Court and table versions use different equipment. The clues identify which version is meant when a cue, a disc, or a weighted puck appears, and avoid assuming one scoring system fits every version.
solvingTip: Read the version named in the clue. The shared sliding action connects the scene, but the equipment words are more specific.
words: Long pushing stick used in court shuffleboard
Flat round piece pushed along a shuffleboard court
Common name for a weighted sliding piece in table shuffleboard
Long marked playing surface for the outdoor version
Marked scoring area toward which a playing piece slides
Raised playing surface used for the indoor tabletop version
Total of points earned in a shuffleboard round
Painted boundary on a shuffleboard court
To move a playing piece smoothly along the surface
To apply forward force with a court game's cue
Another name for a heavy sliding piece in the table game
One completed sequence of play in court shuffleboard
Single scoring unit in the game

answerNotes.CUE: Court shuffleboard uses a cue to push a disc. Table shuffleboard is normally played by sliding weights by hand.
answerNotes.DISC: Disc identifies the court piece here. The table version uses weighted pieces often called weights or pucks.
answerNotes.PUCK: Puck is used for the table piece in this clue. Terminology varies, and weights is another familiar name.
answerNotes.COURT: Court distinguishes the floor or outdoor game from the smaller tabletop game. Its scoring markings belong to that version.
answerNotes.ZONE: A scoring zone is a region of the surface. Its value and boundaries depend on the version and rules being used.

title: Mini Golf by the Park
description: Follow a miniature-golf course through putting equipment, playful obstacles, and simple scorekeeping words.
cardDescription: Follow a miniature-golf course through putting equipment, playful obstacles, and simple scorekeeping words.
focus: Miniature golf uses short putting holes and often decorative obstacles. The clues keep the course features separate from the score and the individual stroke.
solvingTip: Picture the path of the ball. A tool, a target opening, and a barrier each have a different role in reaching the hole.
words: Short form for the putting game played on small obstacle-filled courses
Golf club used to roll the ball toward a nearby hole
Course feature that blocks or complicates the ball's route
Rotating-sail structure often copied as a miniature-golf feature
One counted attempt to hit the golf ball with the club
Covered passage through which a mini-golf ball may roll
Small raised crossing on a themed putting course
One numbered playing section of a miniature-golf course
Recessed target opening that receives the ball
Small round object rolled with a putter
Reference number of strokes assigned to a hole
Recorded number of strokes for a player
Starting area of a miniature-golf hole

answerNotes.MINIGOLF: Mini golf is written without a space in the grid. It is also called miniature golf.
answerNotes.PUTTER: A putter is designed for the putting stroke. It differs from the longer-distance clubs used on a full-size course.
answerNotes.OBSTACLE: An obstacle changes the route or difficulty of a hole. Its decorative appearance does not define the scoring rule.
answerNotes.WINDMILL: A windmill is a familiar themed obstacle. Not every miniature-golf course includes one.
answerNotes.STROKE: Strokes are the basic scoring units. A player's goal is usually to finish a hole in as few as possible under the course's rules.

title: A Pitch of Horseshoes
description: Recognize the equipment and familiar result words used in a recreational game of horseshoes.
cardDescription: Recognize the equipment and familiar result words used in a recreational game of horseshoes.
focus: The game centers on pitching shoes toward a stake. A ringer has a particular position around the stake, while scoring for other positions depends on the rules being followed.
solvingTip: Use the result’s position rather than assuming a point value. Equipment, playing area, and throwing action are separate categories.
words: Thrown horseshoe that surrounds the stake
Horseshoe resting against the stake without surrounding it
U-shaped metal object pitched toward a stake in this game
Upright metal target in a horseshoe pit
To throw a horseshoe toward the target
Prepared landing area around a horseshoe stake
Granular material used in some horseshoe landing areas
Fine-textured material used in many horseshoe pits
Short game term for one of the U-shaped throwing pieces
Unit used to keep score in a horseshoe game
Complete playing area containing the horseshoe targets
Curved path followed by a thrown shoe
Gentle throwing action used in a casual game

answerNotes.RINGER: A ringer encircles the stake under the game's definition. A shoe merely leaning against it is not automatically a ringer.
answerNotes.LEANER: Leaner describes the shoe's resting position. Its scoring treatment depends on the chosen rules.
answerNotes.HORSESHOE: The game's pitching shoes have a specialized design. The name connects them with the familiar curved protective shoe for a horse's hoof.
answerNotes.STAKE: The stake is the target. The pit is the surrounding landing area.
answerNotes.PITCH: Pitch names the action in this sport. It has different meanings in music and in other games.

title: A Friendly Cribbage Board
description: Explore a traditional card game through its pegged board, counting terms, and the dealer’s extra hand.
cardDescription: Explore a traditional card game through its pegged board, counting terms, and the dealer’s extra hand.
focus: Cribbage combines card combinations with movement along a scoring board. The clues identify familiar standard scoring ideas while avoiding an assumption that every game uses the same target total.
solvingTip: A clue about the board may have a different answer from a clue about the cards. A precise scoring total can identify a longer game word.
words: Extra cribbage hand assembled from players' discards for the dealer
Small marker moved through holes in a cribbage board
Card total scoring two points in standard cribbage
Sequence of consecutive card ranks counted in cribbage
Card rank relevant to the cribbage scoring terms nobs and heels
Perforated scoring track used with cribbage pegs
Cards held by one player before being counted
To distribute cards to the players
Complete set of playing cards used for the game
Single rectangular playing piece bearing a rank and suit
Two cards of equal rank counted together
To add the value of scoring card combinations
Number of points a player has earned
Small opening receiving a peg in the board
To reach the game's agreed scoring goal

answerNotes.CRIB: The crib belongs to the dealer for scoring. It is separate from the cards retained in each player's own hand.
answerNotes.PEG: Pegs show scoring progress. Using successive positions helps display the current and preceding score.
answerNotes.FIFTEEN: In standard cribbage, combinations totaling fifteen score two points. The clue names the total rather than the points awarded.
answerNotes.RUN: A run uses consecutive ranks. It is different from a pair of cards sharing the same rank.
answerNotes.JACK: These familiar terms concern a jack in specific positions. Their conditions differ, so the clue asks only for the rank.
